messages.text: Djokovic creates more history with epic Zverev win at China Open

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday.
metadata.content: China Open: Novak Djokovic keeps unblemished record in Beijing by handing Alexander Zverev a rare defeat | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open: Novak Djokovic keeps unblemished record in Beijing by handing Alexander Zverev a rare defeat Novak Djokovic preserves his unblemished record in Beijing by downing in-form Alexander Zverev to set up a semi-final showdown with Daniil Medvedev; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Sunday 4 October 2026 15:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev served up an unbelievable rally during their clash at the China Open Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday. The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing. With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open. messages.text: Daryz retains Arc crown with dazzling display

metadata.summary: Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp.
metadata.content: Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe: Daryz becomes first colt since 1978 to retain Group 1 crown | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe: Daryz becomes first colt since 1978 to retain Group 1 crown The Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz became the first colt since 1978 to retain his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown with a magnificent performance at ParisLongchamp; Bay City Roller finished runner-up, with Diamond Necklace third Sunday 4 October 2026 16:20, UK Image: Daryz won the 2026 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp. Not since the Vincent O'Brien-trained Alleged and Lester Piggott in 1977 and 1978 has a colt managed to defend his title, but once Mickael Barzalona pulled the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz out to make his run the result looked inevitable. The Prix Foy proved the key form guide, as Daryz beat George Scott's Bay City Roller in that trial and those two filled the same positions again in the main event, with Aidan O'Brien's Diamond Necklace running a fine race in third from stall 16. Barzalona said: "To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse. metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton said he was pushing to start on intermediate tyres before the choice of a slick compound led to a disastrous beginning to the Bahrain Grand Prix for Ferrari.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver reveals debate that preceded disastrous tyre choice at start of Bahrain GP in Malaysia | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver reveals debate that preceded disastrous tyre choice at start of Bahrain GP in Malaysia Lewis Hamilton dropped from second on the grid to near the rear of the field after Ferrari opted to start on slick tyres in wet conditions at the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix; Hamilton fought back to claim a podium amid further strategy debate during the race Sunday 4 October 2026 15:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reveals his heart sank when Ferrari chose to start on soft tyres while the majority of other cars started on intermediates Lewis Hamilton said he was pushing to start on intermediate tyres before the choice of a slick compound led to a disastrous beginning to the Bahrain Grand Prix for Ferrari. Hamilton had qualified second on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit - with Malaysia hosting the race amid ongoing conflict in the Middle East - but his hopes of victory were blown as Ferrari chose to start both him and team-mate Charles Leclerc on soft slick tyres in the hope that the wet track would quickly dry out once the cars took to it. metadata.summary: Max Verstappen overcame a chaotic, twice-delayed, rain-affected race to claim his first win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli strengthened his title bid with second place as George Russell retired late on.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen wins first race of 2026 F1 season in wild, rain-hit Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton surges back | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen wins first race of 2026 F1 season in wild, rain-hit Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton surges back Torrential rain, lengthy race-start delay, formation lap chaos, botched tyre gambles and Safety Cars contribute to a remarkable day at Sepang; Max Verstappen ends Red Bull's wait for another win; Kimi Antonelli's extends title lead to 84 points after engine fault forces George Russell out Sunday 4 October 2026 15:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit. Max Verstappen overcame a chaotic, twice-delayed, rain-affected race to claim his first win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli strengthened his title bid with second place as George Russell retired late on. Formula 1's return to Sepang after a nine-year absence produced the most remarkable race day of the season, with heavy rain before the start finally delivering the campaign's first wet-weather action at its 16th round. The start time was twice pushed back by delays before the 55 laps were twice disrupted by Safety Cars. Verstappen beat Antonelli to victory, while Lewis Hamilton stunningly fought back from dropping to 18th after a Ferrari tyre-strategy gamble backfired

Sunday 4 October 2026 14:06, UK Image: Amusingly wins the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Cal Sport Media via AP Images) Amusingly oozed class in beating the colts to land the Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere at ParisLongchamp. Francis-Henri Graffard surprised many when switching his Juddmonte-owned filly from the Prix Marcel Boussac against her own sex, but the decision was well and truly vindicated. Colin Keane dropped his mount out last in the early stages and she tracked the odds-on favourite Folsom Blues, with both travelling ominously well. Joseph O'Brien's National Stakes winner had no answer to the finishing burst of Amusingly, though, and the daughter of No Nay Never pulled away to win in tremendous fashion. Graffard said: "She beat the filly that finished second in the Marcel Boussac (Data) very easily, so I was hoping I didn't make a mistake. metadata.summary: The FIA revealed an “unprecedented” glitch caused several cars to stop in the chaotic start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
metadata.content: FIA explain 'unprecedented' glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia start chaos on formation laps | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content FIA explain 'unprecedented' glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia start chaos on formation laps The formation laps at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely; watch the Singapore GP Sprint weekend from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 4 October 2026 15:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit The FIA revealed an “unprecedented” glitch caused several cars to stop in the chaotic start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Heavy rain in Sepang caused a delayed start but when the drivers left the pit lane, multiple drivers almost grinded to a halt including race leader Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton with several drivers in the midfield also experiencing issues. The start procedure was abandoned and the Grand Prix eventually started properly with the original grid order almost an hour after the carnage. Hull FC-bound Daly Cherry-Evans kicked the crucial drop goal as the Sydney Roosters held on by one point to break Newcastle Knights hearts in a dramatic NRL Grand Final. The Roosters overturned a 12-point deficit to deny Newcastle a fairytale ending to their Cinderella season and claim a 16th premiership after a thrilling Grand Final in Sydney. Inspirational captain, James Tedesco, and a show-stopping performance from Mark Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at ‌both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, handed the Red White and Bluesters their first title since 2019.
